commit.message:
fix(gpu-sig-verifier): build standalone; record the k256 dependency in Cargo.lock

- The crate serializes String and Vec but enabled serde without std, so it
  only compiled when some other workspace member unified serde's std feature
  in: cargo test -p gpu-sig-verifier failed with 10 E0277 errors, on master
  too.
- The CPU reference verifier added k256 to Cargo.toml without the matching
  Cargo.lock edge, so every --locked build of this branch failed.

tests: cargo test -p gpu-sig-verifier --locked -> 5 passed; cargo metadata --locked -> ok

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
feat(lang): structs in X3 source, compiled to the chain; tuple `t.0` access (#622)

struct Point { x: i64, y: i64 }
let mut p = Point { y: 2, x: 1 };  p.x = p.x + p.y;  f(p);  return p;

- Parser: `struct` items, struct literals (not in an if/while condition unless
  parenthesised, Rust's rule), `s.f = v`, and `t.0` / `t.0 = v` for tuples. The condition
  parser no longer stops after a parenthesised operand (`if (a) == b {` used to fail).
- Type checker: nominal struct types, resolved in dependency order; refuses unknown,
  duplicate and recursive structs, unknown field types, missing/extra/repeated fields in a
  literal, field type mismatches, writes through an immutable binding.
- Lowering: a struct value is a tuple of its fields in declaration order; field reads are
  constant-position element reads; `s.f = v` rebinds `s` (value semantics, like `a[i] = v`)
  through a new FIELD_SET intrinsic the backend emits as `store_field` with the position as
  an immediate. A literal's fields are evaluated in the order written, through temporaries
  when that differs from declaration order.
- Tests: end-to-end on the chain engine (functions taking and returning structs, nested
  structs holding arrays, loops updating fields, evaluation order, value semantics, a
  struct returned from main), 15 refusal cases, condition/literal disambiguation; struct
  programs added to the never-panics fuzz seeds.
